data.summary: The eight‑week plan systematically covers all AP Physics 1 units, allocating the 6 hours each week to a balanced mix of instruction, practice, and review. Live classes are slotted in their designated weeks, and the final two weeks focus on comprehensive review and timed exam practice.

weeks.focus: Introduce basic kinematics and build vector intuition.
tasks: Watch live Class 10300 and take detailed notes on scalars/vectors and displacement/velocity.
Do 15 free‑response kinematics questions covering 1.1–1.3; check answers with the scoring guide.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of key equations for 1.1–1.3.

weeks.focus: Complete kinematics and begin force fundamentals.
tasks: Solve 10 problems on reference frames and two‑dimensional motion (1.4‑1.5).
Draw free‑body diagrams for 5 different systems (2.1‑2.2).
Complete a worksheet converting linear to vector quantities for 2.1‑2.2.

weeks.focus: Energy concepts and integrate live class material.
tasks: Attend live Class 10301; focus on translational kinetic energy and energy conservation.
Do 12 mixed‑topic problems on work, potential energy, and conservation (3.1‑3.4).
Answer 5 free‑response questions on Newton's third and first laws (2.3‑2.4).
Summarize the relationship between work and energy in a one‑page cheat sheet.

weeks.focus: Complete energy unit and start linear momentum.
tasks: Calculate power for 8 real‑world scenarios (3.5).
Solve 10 impulse‑momentum problems (4.1‑4.2).
Create a concept map linking work, energy, and momentum.

weeks.focus: Linear momentum conservation and introduce rotational kinematics.
tasks: Complete 8 collision problems covering elastic and inelastic cases (4.3‑4.4).
Work through 6 rotational‑kinematics questions (5.1‑5.2).
Write a short explanation of how linear and rotational motion connect (5.2).

weeks.focus: Torque, rotational inertia, and energy of rotating systems.
tasks: Calculate torque and rotational inertia for 5 objects (5.3‑5.4).
Solve 8 problems on rotational kinetic energy and torque‑work (6.1‑6.2).
Create flashcards for all rotational formulas.

weeks.focus: Review oscillations and fluid dynamics; mixed concept reinforcement.
tasks: Do 10 SHM free‑response questions covering all subtopics (7.1‑7.4).
Complete a fluid‑dynamics worksheet on pressure, density, and conservation laws (8.1‑8.4).
Take a 30‑minute timed quiz mixing oscillation and fluid problems.

weeks.focus: Timed full‑exam practice and comprehensive review.
tasks: Take a full‑length AP Physics 1 practice exam under timed conditions.
Score the exam using the official rubric; note any remaining weak spots.
Review incorrect answers and redo those problems with solution guides.

data.final_week_advice: After the timed practice, focus on the few topics that still feel shaky; do targeted drills for those areas, and keep reviewing your summary sheets daily up to the exam day.
